# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*The following is Angular's official best-practices rules file, included verbatim from
<https://angular.dev/assets/context/best-practices.md>. It is part of the Angular
architecture.*

You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

### Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components

package net.officefloor.hq.app.person;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.List;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.Audit;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.rollup.Rollups;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.SheetService;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;

/** The people kept on a sheet: listed, added and edited. */
@Service
public class PersonService {

    private final PersonRepository people;
    private final SheetService sheets;
    private final Rollups rollups;
    private final Audit audit;

    public PersonService(PersonRepository people, SheetService sheets, Rollups rollups, Audit audit) {
        this.people = people;
        this.sheets = sheets;
        this.rollups = rollups;
        this.audit = audit;
    }

    /** The sheet's people in the order they were added. */
    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    public List<Person> list(String sheetId) {
        return people.findBySheetIdOrderByIdAsc(sheetId);
    }

    /** Add a person to the sheet; refused when the name is already in use on it. */
    @Transactional
    public Person add(String sheetId, String user, String name, String grade) {
        sheets.load(sheetId);
        requireNameFree(sheetId, name, null);
        Rollups.Rollup before = rollups.take(sheetId);
        Person person = people.saveAndFlush(new Person(sheetId, name, grade));
        audited("PERSON_ADDED", sheetId, user, person, sheets.today(sheetId));
        rollups.audit(sheetId, user, before);
        return person;
    }

    /**
     * Change a person's name and record their grade from a date (null: the sheet's today), keeping the
     * grades already recorded, from the version of the person the editor loaded; refused when someone
     * has saved the person since, or when the name is in use by another person.

content.text:
Watching people now works, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**How it works**
- **Storage:** a new migration (`V41__person_watch.sql`) adds a `person_watch` table: one row per sheet, person and user. Each user can watch a person only once. A row's id records the order users started watching. Unwatching deletes the row, so if someone watches again they go to the end of the order.
- **Server:**
  - `person/WatchService.java` handles watching and unwatching and writes `PERSON_WATCHED` / `PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>`. Watching someone you already watch, or unwatching someone you don't, is refused with an error and nothing is written.
  - There are three new endpoints on `PersonController`: `GET …/people/watched` (the ids of the people the signed-in user watches), `PUT …/people/{id}/watch` and `DELETE …/people/{id}/watch`.
- **Notifications:** `ClaimService` writes one `NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name> number=<number>` line per watcher, in watch order, when a claim is settled, approved or re-settled. The lines go after the claim's own line and before the rollup lines. They are written only if the change commits, like the existing audit lines. Bulk settle goes through the same code, so it notifies too.
  - A clerk's settle that is sent to PENDING instead does not notify.
- **Screen:** each person row has a "Watched" column showing `person-watched` (yes/no for the signed-in user) and a `person-watch` toggle button. A refused toggle shows the row's existing `person-error`, which is cleared when the next action on that row is taken. The watched set is re-read every time the sheet is loaded.

Because the change guard blocks every write from a viewer, viewers can't watch anyone. The request didn't cover viewers, so I left that as it is.
